title: Work & Business
tagline: Communicate clearly throughout your working day.
description: Practice practical workplace English for messages, meetings, deadlines, feedback, customer support, remote teamwork, presentations, and everyday negotiations.

chapters.title: Finding Your Feet
chapters.description: Meet colleagues, understand responsibilities, and ask useful questions at work.

sentences.text: I'll be working with the sales team this month.
sentences.hint: Explain your temporary team assignment.

sentences.text: Could you show me where we keep the office supplies?
sentences.hint: Ask a colleague to help you find shared materials.

sentences.text: My main responsibility is keeping our product information up to date.
sentences.hint: Describe the central task in your role.

sentences.text: Who should I contact if I have a question about expenses?
sentences.hint: Find the right person for advice about work-related costs.

sentences.text: I've used a similar system in my previous role.
sentences.hint: Mention relevant experience from an earlier job.

sentences.text: We usually have a short team meeting on Monday mornings.
sentences.hint: Describe a regular event at the start of the working week.

sentences.text: Is there a guide I can read before the training session?
sentences.hint: Ask for material to help you prepare to learn.

sentences.text: I'm still learning the process, so I may need some help.
sentences.hint: Explain why you might ask colleagues for support.

sentences.text: You've made me feel welcome during my first week.
sentences.hint: Appreciate the team's friendly introduction to your new job.

sentences.text: Let's introduce ourselves before we begin the workshop.
sentences.hint: Suggest that participants share who they are before an activity.

chapters.title: Messages That Make Sense
chapters.description: Write complete, polite email sentences that make the next step clear.

sentences.text: I'm writing to confirm our appointment for Tuesday afternoon.
sentences.hint: State that a planned meeting is still going ahead.

sentences.text: Please find the updated schedule attached to this email.
sentences.hint: Direct the reader to a revised document included with your message.

sentences.text: Could you send me the order number so I can check its status?
sentences.hint: Request the detail needed to investigate a purchase.

sentences.text: Thank you for getting back to me so quickly.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge a prompt response.

sentences.text: I've copied our finance team into this conversation.
sentences.hint: Explain that colleagues responsible for money matters can also see the messages.

sentences.text: Would you prefer a phone call or a written summary?
sentences.hint: Offer a choice of communication methods.

sentences.text: The link in my earlier email was incorrect, and I apologize for the confusion.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge a mistake in a previous message.

sentences.text: For clarity, the price includes delivery but not installation.
sentences.hint: Explain exactly which services are covered by a quoted amount.

sentences.text: Please let me know by noon whether you can attend.
sentences.hint: Request confirmation of availability before a specific time.

sentences.text: I'll follow up next week if I haven't heard from you.
sentences.hint: Explain when you will contact the reader again without a reply.

chapters.title: Meetings With a Purpose
chapters.description: Open a discussion, contribute ideas, and finish with clear actions.

sentences.text: The aim of today's meeting is to choose a launch date.
sentences.hint: Explain the decision the group needs to make.

sentences.text: Does anyone have an update before we move to the next item?
sentences.hint: Invite new information before continuing the agenda.

sentences.text: I'd like to hear from the people who handle deliveries.
sentences.hint: Ask for input from colleagues with relevant practical experience.

sentences.text: Could you give us an example of the problem?
sentences.hint: Request a specific case to make an issue clearer.

sentences.text: That's a useful point, but we need to stay within our budget.
sentences.hint: Recognize an idea while reminding the group about spending limits.

sentences.text: We seem to be discussing two separate questions.
sentences.hint: Point out that different topics have become mixed together.

sentences.text: Shall we take five minutes to compare the options?
sentences.hint: Suggest a brief pause to consider the alternatives.

sentences.text: I'm happy to take notes while you lead the discussion.
sentences.hint: Offer to record the meeting as someone else runs it.

sentences.text: Before we finish, let's confirm who is doing each task.
sentences.hint: Check responsibilities at the end of a meeting.

sentences.text: We've agreed to test the new process with a small group first.
sentences.hint: Summarize a decision to begin with a limited trial.

chapters.title: Time, Tasks, and Deadlines
chapters.description: Discuss progress, manage priorities, and raise timing concerns early.

sentences.text: The report is due on Friday, and the research is nearly complete.
sentences.hint: Share both a deadline and the current state of the work.

sentences.text: Which of these requests should I deal with first?
sentences.hint: Ask someone to help you set priorities.

sentences.text: I can finish the draft today if the figures arrive this morning.
sentences.hint: Explain what you need in order to complete a task on time.

sentences.text: We need to allow extra time for the final checks.
sentences.hint: Recommend leaving room in the schedule for review.

sentences.text: I'm waiting for approval before I place the order.
sentences.hint: Explain why a purchase cannot go ahead yet.

sentences.text: Could we move the deadline back by two days?
sentences.hint: Request a short extension.

sentences.text: The design changes are taking longer than we expected.
sentences.hint: Warn that part of the project is using more time than planned.

sentences.text: Let's divide the work so that no one has too much to do.
sentences.hint: Suggest sharing tasks more evenly across the team.

sentences.text: I'll let you know straight away if the delivery date changes.
sentences.hint: Promise a prompt warning about any change in arrival time.

sentences.text: We've completed the urgent tasks, so we can focus on next week's plans.
sentences.hint: Explain that immediate work is done and attention can shift.

chapters.title: Feedback That Helps
chapters.description: Recognize strengths, suggest improvements, and respond constructively to advice.

sentences.text: Your explanation made a difficult topic easy to understand.
sentences.hint: Praise someone's clear communication.

sentences.text: Could you make the introduction shorter and add a clear example?
sentences.hint: Request two specific improvements to a piece of work.

sentences.text: The layout looks good, although the headings are hard to read.
sentences.hint: Balance a positive comment with a concern about readability.

sentences.text: What would you suggest I do differently next time?
sentences.hint: Ask for advice that could improve future performance.

sentences.text: I appreciate the feedback, and I'll revise the document this afternoon.
sentences.hint: Accept advice and explain how you will act on it.

sentences.text: It would help if you checked the totals before sharing the file.
sentences.hint: Recommend a practical habit to prevent number errors.

sentences.text: You've become much more confident when answering questions.
sentences.hint: Recognize a colleague's progress in speaking with others.

sentences.text: Can we discuss the feedback in private after lunch?
sentences.hint: Request a more suitable setting for a sensitive conversation.

sentences.text: I understand the concern, but I'd like to explain why I chose this approach.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge criticism while asking to share your reasoning.

sentences.text: Let's agree on one improvement to focus on this week.
sentences.hint: Turn feedback into a manageable short-term goal.

chapters.title: Taking Care of Customers
chapters.description: Clarify customer needs, handle problems calmly, and offer practical solutions.

sentences.text: What will you mainly use the equipment for?
sentences.hint: Ask about a customer's needs before recommending a product.

sentences.text: This model costs less to run, but it takes up more space.
sentences.hint: Compare an operating advantage with a practical drawback.

sentences.text: Let me check that I've understood your request correctly.
sentences.hint: Confirm the details before taking action.

sentences.text: I'm sorry the parcel arrived later than we promised.
sentences.hint: Apologize for failing to meet an agreed delivery time.

sentences.text: Could you describe what happens when you switch the device on?
sentences.hint: Ask for an observation that may help identify a fault.

sentences.text: I'll stay on the line while you try those steps.
sentences.hint: Offer continued support during a phone troubleshooting call.

sentences.text: We can offer a replacement or return the full amount you paid.
sentences.hint: Give a customer two ways to resolve a faulty purchase.

sentences.text: I don't have that information yet, but I'll find out for you.
sentences.hint: Be honest about a knowledge gap and offer to investigate.

sentences.text: Would you like me to explain the return policy before you decide?
sentences.hint: Offer useful conditions to support a purchase decision.

sentences.text: Thank you for your patience while we sorted out the problem.
sentences.hint: Appreciate a customer's understanding during a delay.

chapters.title: Working Together From Anywhere
chapters.description: Coordinate across locations, share work clearly, and handle online meeting issues.

sentences.text: Can everyone hear me clearly, or should I use a headset?
sentences.hint: Check your sound quality at the start of an online call.

sentences.text: Your screen is frozen, but we can still hear your voice.
sentences.hint: Describe a video problem without suggesting the whole connection has failed.

sentences.text: I'll share my screen so we can look at the same document.
sentences.hint: Offer a common view of the material under discussion.

sentences.text: Please put your questions in the chat while the speaker is presenting.
sentences.hint: Suggest a way to ask questions without interrupting.

sentences.text: I've saved the latest version in our shared folder.
sentences.hint: Tell colleagues where to find the current file.

sentences.text: Could we choose a time that suits colleagues in both time zones?
sentences.hint: Request a meeting schedule that considers different locations.

sentences.text: I won't be online tomorrow morning, but I've left detailed notes.
sentences.hint: Explain an absence and how others can continue without you.

sentences.text: A written update would save us from arranging another call.
sentences.hint: Suggest a simpler alternative to an extra meeting.

sentences.text: Let's check with the team before recording the session.
sentences.hint: Recommend getting agreement before saving an online conversation.

sentences.text: If your connection drops, you can rejoin using the same link.
sentences.hint: Explain how to return after an internet interruption.

chapters.title: Presenting an Idea
chapters.description: Guide an audience through information, explain evidence, and handle questions.

sentences.text: Today I'd like to show you a simpler way to manage bookings.
sentences.hint: Introduce a presentation about improving a routine task.

sentences.text: I'll begin with the main problem and then explain our proposed solution.
sentences.hint: Give the audience a clear outline of your talk.

sentences.text: As this chart shows, most orders arrive during the first week of each month.
sentences.hint: Use a visual to describe a regular pattern in sales.

sentences.text: Compared with last year, we've reduced the average waiting time.
sentences.hint: Describe an improvement by comparing two periods.

sentences.text: The main benefit for customers is that they can book without calling us.
sentences.hint: Explain how a proposed service makes life easier for users.

sentences.text: Let me give you an example from a typical working day.
sentences.hint: Introduce a realistic situation to support an explanation.

sentences.text: We tested the idea with ten users, so the results are still limited.
sentences.hint: Explain why early evidence should be treated cautiously.

sentences.text: That's an important question, and the next slide should help answer it.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge an audience question that your upcoming material addresses.

sentences.text: To sum up, this change could save time without increasing costs.
sentences.hint: Close by highlighting efficiency and affordability.

sentences.text: What concerns would you want us to address before we move forward?
sentences.hint: Invite the audience to identify issues before a decision.

chapters.title: Finding a Fair Agreement
chapters.description: Discuss prices and conditions, offer alternatives, and confirm an agreement.

sentences.text: Before we discuss the price, could we confirm exactly what the service includes?
sentences.hint: Clarify the offer before negotiating its cost.

sentences.text: Our budget is limited, but we're interested in a longer contract.
sentences.hint: Balance a spending restriction with a possible benefit for the supplier.

sentences.text: Would a larger order allow you to offer a lower price per item?
sentences.hint: Ask whether buying more could earn a discount.

sentences.text: We could accept a later delivery if transport were included in the price.
sentences.hint: Offer flexibility on timing in exchange for a cost benefit.

sentences.text: That offer is close to what we need, although the payment date is difficult.
sentences.hint: Identify the remaining concern in an otherwise suitable proposal.

sentences.text: Is there any flexibility in the length of the trial period?
sentences.hint: Explore whether a testing arrangement can be adjusted.

sentences.text: I'd need approval from my manager before agreeing to that amount.
sentences.hint: Explain the limit of your authority to accept a price.

sentences.text: Rather than reduce the quality, we suggest starting with fewer products.
sentences.hint: Offer a smaller quantity as an alternative to a lower standard.

sentences.text: Let's put the agreed terms in writing so both sides have a clear record.
sentences.hint: Recommend documenting the deal to avoid confusion.

sentences.text: We're pleased to have found an arrangement that works for both companies.
sentences.hint: End a negotiation by recognizing a balanced outcome.

chapters.title: When Plans Need to Change
chapters.description: Handle setbacks responsibly, explain trade-offs, and learn from completed work.

sentences.text: We've found an error in the estimate, and I'd like to explain the impact.
sentences.hint: Raise a mistake openly and prepare to discuss its consequences.

sentences.text: The supplier can't provide all the materials, so we need an alternative.
sentences.hint: Describe a shortage that requires a different plan.

sentences.text: What can we deliver on time without putting quality at risk?
sentences.hint: Ask how to meet commitments while protecting standards.

sentences.text: I should have raised this issue earlier, and I take responsibility for the delay.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge that your late warning affected the schedule.

sentences.text: Let's inform the customer now rather than wait until the last minute.
sentences.hint: Recommend giving early notice of a problem.

sentences.text: If we postpone the launch, we'll have more time for testing but miss the holiday sales.
sentences.hint: Explain both a benefit and a cost of changing the schedule.

sentences.text: Could someone check my calculations before I send the revised figures?
sentences.hint: Request a second review to prevent another numerical mistake.

sentences.text: The immediate problem is solved, but we still need to understand its cause.
sentences.hint: Distinguish fixing an issue from learning why it happened.

sentences.text: Looking back, clearer instructions would have prevented most of the confusion.
sentences.hint: Identify a communication improvement after reviewing past work.

sentences.text: Before we close the project, let's record what worked well and what we'd change.
sentences.hint: Suggest capturing useful lessons at the end of the work.
